author: Sung on the north coast
pages:
Out of the mist at the turn of the night,
A hull without paint and a sail without light,
She rides on no wind and she leaves no wake,
And her crew pull oars for their own oaths' sake.

Hail her not, sailor, and give her the lee,
For the dead row slow but they never row free;
And when the dawn comes and the grey turns gold,
She is gone like breath on a morning cold.
